tasks.title: Strip stray mutation_target from non-test_authoring tasks in normalize_plan
acceptance_criteria: A new pure module-level helper `_strip_stray_mutation_targets(tasks)` is added to `harness/planner/plan_normalizer.py`, placed after the other small `_helpers`, that deletes the scalar `mutation_target` key in place from every task whose final meta_task_type is NOT `test_authoring`.
The helper reuses the existing `_is_test_authoring(task)` (does NOT reimplement it) and guards each entry with `isinstance(t, dict)` and `'mutation_target' in t`.

`normalize_plan` calls `_strip_stray_mutation_targets(normalized['tasks'])` as its FINAL pass — after `normalized = _inject_oracle_sources(normalized, repo_root)` and immediately before `return normalized` — guarded by `isinstance(normalized.get('tasks'), list)`.
The pre-committed RED oracle `tests/planner/test_strip_stray_mutation_target.py` is GREEN and no existing planner test regresses under `python -m pytest tests/planner/ -q`.

No new imports are added (`List`, `Dict`, `Any` are already imported); no I/O, network, clock, or randomness is introduced; `mutations[]` handling is untouched; only the scalar `mutation_target` key is affected.

Only `harness/planner/plan_normalizer.py` is modified; the patch is a `__JANUSMASK_PATCHES__` symbol patch that modifies `normalize_plan` and carries the new top-level `_strip_stray_mutation_targets` as an extra-node symbol, without rewriting unrelated functions.

spec.objective: Enforce the planner-schema invariant 'Omit mutation_target for all non-test_authoring tasks' deterministically inside `normalize_plan` by adding a single new pure pass `_strip_stray_mutation_targets` that drops a stray scalar `mutation_target` from every non-test_authoring task, while preserving it on genuine `test_authoring` oracles. This closes a real defect: the blind planner reflexively attaches `mutation_target = "<module>.<function>"` to NEW-FILE implementation/data_model tasks; downstream the orchestrator non-vacuity mutation gate triggers on that stray field, maps the dotted value to a path via `value.replace('.', '/') + '.py'` (e.g. `ngv2/source_localize/localize_source.py`, which does not exist — the real module is `ngv2/source_localize.py` and `localize_source` is a function inside it), and fail-closes the task with `mutation_gate_error`.
functional_requirements: Add a top-level pure helper `def _strip_stray_mutation_targets(tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None` that iterates `tasks` and, for each `t` where `isinstance(t, dict)` and `not _is_test_authoring(t)` and `'mutation_target' in t`, executes `del t['mutation_target']`, mutating the list in place and returning None.

Wire the helper as the FINAL pass of `normalize_plan`: after `normalized = _inject_oracle_sources(normalized, repo_root)`, add `if isinstance(normalized.get('tasks'), list): _strip_stray_mutation_targets(normalized['tasks'])` immediately before `return normalized`, so the strip runs on the FINAL meta_task_type (after `_correct_meta_task_type_by_target`).
Preserve `mutation_target` verbatim on tasks whose final meta_task_type is `test_authoring`, since the non-vacuity gate legitimately needs it there.

Remain pure and deterministic: rely on the existing top-level `normalized = copy.deepcopy(plan)` so the caller's input is never mutated; add no new imports, no I/O, no network, no clock, no randomness; touch only the scalar `mutation_target` key and not `mutations[]`.
spec.interfaces: harness/planner/plan_normalizer.py: add `_strip_stray_mutation_targets(tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None` (in-place over the tasks list, reusing `_is_test_authoring`) and call it as the last pass inside `normalize_plan(plan, repo_root=None)` right before `return normalized`, guarded by `isinstance(normalized.get('tasks'), list)`.
edge_cases: Stray `mutation_target` on an `implementation` task is stripped.
Stray `mutation_target` on a `data_model` task is stripped.
`normalize_plan` does not mutate its input and the strip is idempotent (double-apply yields an equal result).
Non-dict entries in the tasks list and tasks lacking a `mutation_target` key are left untouched (no KeyError, no crash).
non_goals: integration is out of scope: do not add any wiring beyond the single call inside `normalize_plan`.
Do not author tests — the RED oracle is pre-committed at JM `db7a9ca`.
Do not change the orchestrator mutation gate, the plan_validator, the blind_draft prompt, or any normalizer pass other than adding the one new helper and its single call site.
Do not touch any file other than `harness/planner/plan_normalizer.py`, and do not touch `mutations[]` handling — only the scalar `mutation_target` key.
spec.implementation_notes: Insert the helper after the other small `_helpers` (e.g. near `_is_test_authoring` around line 46). Use the exact body from the brief: `for t in tasks: if isinstance(t, dict) and (not _is_test_authoring(t)) and ('mutation_target' in t): del t['mutation_target']`. The wiring goes after `normalized = _inject_oracle_sources(normalized, repo_root)` (around line 1025) and before `return normalized` (line 1026). `normalize_plan` already deep-copies at the top, so in-place mutation of `normalized['tasks']` keeps the no-mutation/idempotency oracle green. Emit a `__JANUSMASK_PATCHES__` symbol patch that modifies `normalize_plan` and carries `_strip_stray_mutation_targets` as an additional extra-node symbol; do not rewrite unrelated functions.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: No new tests to author — the pre-committed oracle `tests/planner/test_strip_stray_mutation_target.py` (JM master `db7a9ca`) is the source of truth. It supplies: a plan with one `implementation` task carrying stray `mutation_target='ngv2.foo.bar'`; the same fixture flipped to `data_model`; a `test_authoring` task with `mutation_target='harness.planner.x'` that must be preserved; and a deep-copied fixture asserting input is unchanged and a second `normalize_plan` application is equal (idempotent). The whole `tests/planner/` suite must stay green to prove no regression.

token_budget_ratio.note: Tiny single-helper edit plus one call site; the oracle is pre-committed so no test authoring is needed, but test_tokens is kept >= 1.5x impl to satisfy the budget invariant and cover running/triaging the full planner suite.
